proof:
# Strict-midpoint local exclusion for arbitrary planar polytopal fibers

## Theorem

Let K0,K1,K2 be positive-area convex polygons in R^2 with

    (K0+K2)/2 contained in int(K1).

Let C be the convex hull of their copies at integer coordinates0,1,2, and
S=C intersect (Z x R^2). These are its exact three fibers. If the family is
a local minimum of maximum normalized ambient halfspace depth under nearby
independent affine changes of the three polygons, then

    max_(y in S) depth_S(y)>=2/9.

The affine variations are actual admissible bodies because strict midpoint
containment is open. The theorem includes oblique caps, boundary coincidences
on other fibers, and nonunique or non-sharp maximizing points. Its conclusion
forces any bad attained polytopal extremizer with three positive planar
fibers onto an active midpoint-compatibility constraint.

## 1. At most one endpoint can be deepest

Write a_z=area(Kz), M=sum a_z, and

    A(K)=max_(y in K) min_H area(K intersect H),

where H ranges over closed planar halfspaces containing y. The ordinary
Grünbaum theorem gives A(K)>=gamma area(K), gamma=4/9. The endpoint fibers
can be isolated by a sufficiently large integer tilt, so their exact
restricted unnormalized maxima are A(K0) and A(K2).

The elementary theorem in candidate 2d61091414784568 proves

    A((K+L)/2)^(1/2)>=(A(K)^(1/2)+A(L)^(1/2))/2,

and A strictly increases under strict containment. For completeness, choose
deepest centers of K,L; for every normal the Minkowski average of their
containing caps lies in the corresponding average-body cap. Ordinary
Brunn--Minkowski gives the displayed inequality simultaneously in every
direction. Strict containment permits an added epsilon ball, whose positive
cap depth yields strict increase by the same inequality.

Thus if the two endpoints were both globally deepest with unnormalized
value D, the middle's own-fiber guarantee would be
A(K1)>A((K0+K2)/2)>=D, a contradiction. At most one endpoint is deepest.
The middle is deepest at any local minimum: otherwise a slight enlargement
of K1 increases M, strictly decreases both endpoint normalized maxima, and
leaves the middle below the former maximum by its strict gap and continuity.

## 2. A finite exact cover and its normalized stress

At an interior restricted maximizer of the middle fiber, take a minimal
positive circuit of active continuous cap normals. There are two or three
caps, with common mass beta M, through one middle point c_*. Here beta is the
global maximum. The previously proved compact cap-capacity lemma gives cap
attainment and the positive circuit. The middle point is interior: a boundary
support normal u satisfies h0(u)+h2(u)<2h1(u), so an integer tilt between
h0-h1 and h1-h2 isolates its zero-area support face. Interior points have
positive depth from their own fiber, so a positive maximizer cannot be on
that boundary.

At each endpoint take an ordinary active continuous-normal circuit at its
own continuous deepest point, and add a large integer tilt strictly excluding
the other two fibers. Each endpoint cap has mass A(Kz). All three groups
cover their whole own continuous fibers, independently of the shapes there.
At nondeep endpoints these budgets are strictly below beta M.

Use independent affine body parameters, and allow cap integer normals and
thresholds to vary with their continuous normals and positive circuit weights
fixed. For a group anchored at z impose the linear condition

    sum_j rho_j(v_j z-b_j)>=0.

This guarantees that group still covers the entire fiber over z. Hence the
base family is a local maximum of total area under these coverage constraints
and fixed cap budgets beta M_0: a larger feasible mass would give actual depth
at most beta M_0/M<beta.

The finite-dimensional normalized separation argument in the joint-cap notes
applies. There are nonnegative cap multipliers lambda, zero on slack caps,
and nonnegative coverage multipliers. No body compatibility multipliers occur,
because independent affine changes are admissible in an open neighborhood.
To check the constraint qualification for arbitrary polygons, shrink each
polygon homothetically about an interior point. Its outward velocity is
strictly negative on every facet. Every active cap's own anchor fiber has a
positive boundary patch lying in the open cap. Thus EVERY generalized cap
gradient has strictly negative pairing with this direction. At a coincident
facet its shape trace lies in [0,1], so it contributes a nonpositive term.
Compactness of the finite gradient-moment sets and separation now normalize
the objective coefficient exactly as in compressed-joint-cap-stress.md.

These cap traces may depend measurably on the point of a coincident edge.
They have the same choices in shape and cap-parameter derivatives. The
objective itself is differentiable under affine body changes.

Joint homothety of all bodies and all cap integer normals/thresholds scales
M and every cap mass by the square factor, while active homogeneous coverage
constraints remain zero. Therefore

    sum_all lambda_j=1/beta.                                     (1)

Only the middle group and at most one endpoint group carry nonzero lambda.

## 3. The middle group has total multiplier at most9/4

Put c_*=0. Let C_j,S_j,X_j be the middle area, section length and section
first moment of its j-th active cap, with unit continuous normal u_j.
All these are proper cuts in K1. Endpoint isolating caps exclude K1 strictly,
so only the middle group contributes to its independent affine stationarity.
Exactly as in the triangle proof, translation and arbitrary linear changes
of K1 give

    sum_j lambda_j S_j u_j=0,
    sum_j lambda_j C_j=area(K1),
    sum_j lambda_j X_j u_j^T=0.                                  (2)

One direct derivation is that under x -> (I+B)x+c the cap derivative is
tr(B)C_j+u_j.B X_j+S_j u_j.c. The section lies on u_j.x=0, so taking B=I
removes its moment term, and the remaining matrix equations give (2).
Minimality of the circuit and the positive middle-area equation imply every
middle multiplier is positive.

If there are two caps, their normals are opposite and their sections coincide.
The weights are equal by the first equation, and their caps partition the
polygon up to a null line. Their multiplier sum is2.

For three caps, the normals have rank2 with a one-dimensional relation space.
The first and third equations in (2) imply that all section midpoints X_j/S_j
are the same. Since they lie on the three concurrent cap lines, this common
midpoint is0. Put L=sum_j lambda_j and theta_j=lambda_j/L. If R is rotation
through pi/2, set

    p_j=-R(u_j) S_j/2.

The chord endpoints are precisely ±p_j, its cap has normal R(p_j) parallel
to u_j with a positive scalar, and sum theta_j p_j=0. The proved sharp theorem
in candidate c22519c29667168e applies to the arbitrary
convex polygon K1 and yields

    sum_j theta_j C_j>=gamma area(K1).

The middle-area equation in (2) gives the left side as area(K1)/L. Hence,
including the two-cap case,

    sum_middle lambda_j<=1/gamma=9/4.                            (3)

No triangle-specific cap shape is used in this step.

## 4. The remaining endpoint group has the same bound

If endpoint e is deepest, its selected ordinary active caps through its own
deepest point each have mass A(Ke)=delta_e area(Ke), where delta_e>=gamma.
Independently dilate Ke about that interior point. Its area derivative is
2 area(Ke), and each of its own through-point caps has derivative2 A(Ke).

Every middle cap generalized shape derivative under this expansion is
nonnegative. On a usual facet the coefficient is the cap's open-facet area;
on a coincident facet it is a nonnegative measurable trace. The outward
homothety velocity about an interior point is positive on every facet.
Holding cap parameters fixed contributes no cap-motion term. Thus normalized
stationarity gives

    2 area(Ke)>=2 A(Ke) sum_endpoint lambda_j,

so

    sum_endpoint lambda_j<=1/delta_e<=1/gamma.                    (4)

There is no endpoint contribution if both are nondeep. Combining (1), (3),
and (4) gives 1/beta<=2/gamma, proving beta>=2/9.

## Exact scope

The new conclusion is an extremal boundary reduction in the three-fiber
planar setting. It does not eliminate active midpoint-contact stresses, and
it does not extend the weighted planar chord theorem to continuous dimension
at least3. The proof uses actual whole-fiber covers and a single deterministic
maximizing point only as a base for each circuit; it never replaces S by its
convex hull when evaluating mixed area.
